summary: Remote new-hire created duplicate Okta/SCIM identities -> duplicate service accounts and device shipped to wrong address
description:
Issue summary:
During automated HR->Okta SCIM sync for a remote new hire (employee_id: 105224), two Okta user objects were created: one with the canonical company email (jane.doe@redwood.ai) and a second temporary object with the HR alternate email (jane.d@contractors.redwood.ai). The provisioning pipeline created service accounts and provisioned a work laptop for both objects. One laptop was sent to the contractor address (incorrect) and VPN conditional access failed for the canonical account because group membership lived on the duplicate object.

Impact:
- New hire cannot complete first-day tasks due to VPN and GitHub access gaps.
- Unnecessary device shipped to wrong address (logistics + security risk).
- Excess service accounts created, increasing audit surface and license consumption.

Environment:
- Identity provider: Okta (SCIM mapping from Workday HRIS).
- Provisioning pipeline: onboard-scripts (k8s job in prod/us-west).
- Asset management: asset-shipper (US logistics partner).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create HR record with primary_email = jane.doe@redwood.ai and alternate_email = jane.d@contractors.redwood.ai and employee_id = 105224.
2) Trigger daily SCIM sync.
3) Observe Okta creates two user objects when SCIM mapping normalizes preferred_username differently and HRIS contains the alternate_email field.
4) Run onboarding pipeline which looks up by email and, failing to find a single unique match, creates per-object service accounts and kicks off asset order for both entries.

Logs / traces (examples):
- SCIM sync job run 2026-03-10T03:12Z: https://logs.redwood.tools/scim-sync/2026-03-10-03-12 (trace id scim-20260310-03-12-ff7b)
- Okta user objects: okta://org/00u7abcd/user/00u1primary and okta://org/00u7abcd/user/00u2alt (object ids redacted in ticket)
- Provisioning runs: onboard-scripts job id onboard-20260310-7f2a, asset-shipper order id ASH-77321

Investigation notes:
- IAM reviewed Okta objects and confirmed two distinct users exist. The canonical account (email jane.doe@redwood.ai) lacked the onboarding-group membership because the group assignment job matched on Okta object id that was attached to the alt object.
- Provisioning logs show onboarding-script chooses a match by querying Okta for email; because both objects listed emails (primary vs alt), the script returned both and proceeded to create separate service accounts rather than failing fast.
- Asset-shipper accepted two orders because it received two distinct device requests with the same employee_id missing from the payload. The package went to the address associated with the alt object (contractor address).
- Root cause: SCIM mapping allowed multiple user creation when alternate_email exists and preferred_username normalization differed. Provisioning lacked a unique employee_id check and relied solely on email matching.

Temporary mitigations enacted:
- Disabled automatic asset ordering for onboarding runs until dedupe guard is deployed (temporary hold put on asset-shipper queue for onboarding category).
- Manually revoked the duplicate service account created for okta object 00u2alt and removed GitHub/org access and tokens (audit log entries created).
- Contacted logistics partner to intercept and return device ASH-77321; pickup confirmed for 2026-03-11.

Permanent remediation plan / action items:
1) SCIM mapping change: normalize and dedupe by employee_id (Workday employee_id) and canonical email; submit PR to idp-mappings (PR #412). Owner: Identity & SRE. Target: 2026-03-19.
2) Provisioning hardening: onboarding-script must fail fast on ambiguous email matches and prefer employee_id primary key. Add unit and integration tests. Owner: Developer Experience. Target: 2026-03-17.
3) Asset ordering safety: require employee_id and user object id match in payload; reject duplicate orders within 48h. Owner: Logistics integration team. Target: 2026-03-17.
4) Playbook update: add runbook for duplicate identity case with steps to validate primary object, revoke extras, and logistics coordination. Owner: Internal Support. Target: 2026-03-15.
5) HR data hygiene: HR to de-duplicate alternate_email attribute for new hires or ensure canonical_email present at hire intake. Owner: People Ops. Target: immediate process update.

Resolution notes:
- Duplicate Okta object 00u2alt had non-production tokens revoked and removed from org groups.
- Provisioning scripts updated to block asset orders for ambiguous matches and pushed hotfix to onboard-scripts (deployed 2026-03-11). PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-scripts/pull/412; github.com/redwood-inference/asset-shipper/pull/89.
- Asset ASH-77321 intercepted and returned to logistics; replacement device ordered to correct home address and delivered 2026-03-12.
- Playbook entry created: Confluence page https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Duplicate+Identity+Onboarding+Playbook

Follow-ups (open):
- Verify analytics for the next 7 days for any additional duplicate creations (owner: SRE).
- Confirm HR intake form change has rolled out (owner: People Ops).
- Schedule retro across IAM, DevEx, and People Ops to prevent recurrence (owner: Support Lead).
